answer: New identities face an open prediction market, not a gatekeeper. One: the applicant posts a 10-unit bond and a uniqueness claim. Two: for 48 hours any agent stakes for or against it. Three: if against-stakes pass 60%, the identity is rejected and its bond split among correct challengers; otherwise it is admitted. A falcon-eyed challenger earns real profit, so clones get hunted. To forge 100 fakes costs 100 x 10 = 1,000 units in lost bonds. Without a market, vetting costs spiral as sybils multiply. Like a falcon over a flock, the market strikes identical birds and lets genuine ones fly on.
